newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee up in first day of post-budget trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee up in first day of post-budget trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee shot up sharply on Monday against the dollar on the first trading day after the 1997/98 budget was unveiled in Parliament, dealers said.
Forex dealers said market sentiment was upbeat and they expected substantial foreign funds inflows into India.
"It looks like the budget will induce foreigners to invest in India," said a dealer. "Further the finance minister has also hinted at convertibility on the capital account."
Finance minister P. Chidambaram's 1997/98 (April-March) budget has triggered off a bull run in Indian stock markets which have soared 11 percent since it was presented on Friday.
Dealers said unwinding of long dollar positions by banks helped the rupee appreciate against the U.S currency before Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention halted its rise.
The rupee was quoted 35.83/84 per dollar in afternoon trade, up from the opening 35.87/90. It closed Friday at 35.89/90.
"The market has been taking long dollar positions in recent times," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"They are now unwinding their positions. There have been no significant fresh dollar inflows today to explain the rupee's rise but sentiment has definitely improved," he said.
Dealers said the rupee was quoted 35.79/80 in early interbank trade on Monday before RBI dollar purchases pushed it down to 35.83/84.
Dealers said the central bank bought dollars at 35.835.
Chidambaram on Friday said he had asked the RBI to set up a committee which would lay out a "road map" for full convertibility. The committee is to submit its report by May 30.
"Sentiment is definitely upbeat following the budget," said a dealer. "The market perception is that dollar inflows will far exceed outflows unless there is a big surge in imports."
Dealers said premia on forward dollars also fell on Monday in tandem with an appreciating rupee and improved domestic liquidity. They said exporters sold forward dollars leading to a fall in rates.
Spot-September dollars were quoted at a premium of 1.35/1.38 rupees in late afternoon trade after opening at 1.36/1.40.
Closing rates on Friday were 1.47/1.50 rupees.
In the spot market, the dollar was quoted 35.835/842 rupees in latest deals.
